Chapter 10: Practicing Gratitude and Savoring the Present.
Gratitude—it’s one of those ideas that sounds so simple… but let’s be honest, actually practicing it? That can be surprisingly tough. It’s just so easy to zero in on what’s missing, what could be different, or that next thing we think we need. But gratitude is about tuning in to what’s already here—and letting those good moments really soak in.
Picture this: a holiday meal, the table overflowing with food and laughter. For just a little while, everything feels right. The stress and worries of the world kind of melt away, and all that matters is being with the people you care about. Someone lifts their glass and says thank you—not just for the meal, but for the company, for the chance to be together. That feeling? It often lingers, even after the last plate’s been cleared.
But gratitude isn’t only for the big, special moments. It shows up in everyday things too—a warm cup of tea, a favorite song playing on the radio, a smile from a stranger. These are the moments that are easy to overlook. But if you start to notice them, they begin to stack up, creating this quiet sense of abundance, even when life gets a little rough.
There’s a story I love about someone who started a gratitude journal. At first, it felt a little strange—jotting down three good things every day. What’s the point, right? But over time, something shifted. The practice changed the way they looked at the world. Sure, the hard days didn’t just vanish, but somehow, they became easier to handle. And the good days? They felt even sweeter.
Most of us really underestimate how powerful gratitude can be. It doesn’t mean ignoring problems or pretending everything’s perfect. It means making space for joy—even when things are tough.
Lots of people get stuck waiting for happiness, thinking it’s just around the corner. But what if happiness is actually hiding in the present, in those moments we tend to miss?
When you think about it, there’s a certain wisdom in how kids move through the world—delighting in the little things, saying thank you, really savoring the moment. Maybe that’s the real secret to living a richer, more meaningful life.
